title: Implement installed detached uninstall runtime with evidence binding
rawUserRequest: Continue the mandatory Japanese assessment remediation. The installed adopter runtime must provide a real, safe uninstall path rather than a template-only model. Fix the discovered process and capability problem before documentation alignment or release, use the instruction-plan-implementation-acceptance bidirectional traceability mechanism, and complete the Work Item through PR, Hosted CI, merge, lifecycle closure, and branch cleanup.

declaredIntent.summary: Close JA-UNINSTALL-RUNTIME-001 with an installed public facts/proposal/execution flow that is fail-closed, proposal-digest bound, evidence-preserving by default, independently verifiable, and accurately documented and assessed.

outOfScope: Purge execution or deletion of archived governance evidence.
Deletion of project-owned, modified, drifted, unknown-owned, protected, or unlisted paths.
Changing installation, upgrade, rollback, release publication, or branch-protection behavior.
Claiming general Japanese fluency, enterprise compliance, security sandboxing, or identity guarantees.
General three-language documentation alignment, deprecated-asset cleanup, release publication, or final plan cleanup.

riskAssessment.reason: This Work Item introduces a public filesystem-removal executor. It must prove exact proposal identity, confinement, evidence preservation, fail-closed ownership/drift behavior, truthful partial-failure receipts, and installed-payload availability.

executionDecision.reason: The user authorized the ordered corrective work; implementation is confined to repository code and temporary test repositories, while real deletion remains confirmation- and digest-gated.

preReviewWarnings: Review path confinement, symlink handling, proposal canonicalization, and time-of-check/time-of-use behavior.
Review that every non-success result reports actual removed, preserved, missing, and failed paths without claiming completion.
Review installer catalog and Make target parity in a clean adopter fixture.

checkpointPolicy.reason: Record the destructive-boundary design before editing and re-evaluate it against the final implementation.

acceptance: A1: An installed `ai-cockpit-uninstall-facts` entrypoint produces deterministic, repository-relative facts for only catalog-managed runtime paths, records existence/type/digest/ownership evidence, and fails closed on symlinks, path escape, malformed state, drift, or unknown ownership.

A2: `ai-cockpit-uninstall-propose` binds the canonical facts, exact mode, deletion list, preservation list, repository identity, and session to a deterministic proposalDigest; changing any bound field invalidates execution.

A3: An installed `ai-cockpit-uninstall-execute` entrypoint requires an exact confirmed proposal digest, revalidates current facts immediately before mutation, removes only unchanged listed runtime files inside the repository, preserves governance evidence and project-owned paths by default, and never follows symlinks.

A4: Execution is detached from files it may remove, writes its receipt outside the deletion set, verifies post-state, and reports `runtimeRemovalVerified: true` only when every requested removable path is absent and every preserved path remains.
A5: Drift, unknown ownership, missing confirmation, digest mismatch, repository mismatch, replayed/completed receipt, and time-of-check/time-of-use changes produce a fail-closed non-mutating result.

A6: Partial filesystem failure produces a non-success receipt with exact removed, preserved, missing, and failed path evidence plus recovery guidance; it never reports completed or runtimeRemovalVerified.
A7: The facts builder and executor scripts plus their public Make targets are in the installer catalog and work in a clean adopted repository without importing template-only files.

A8: Unit, mutation, path-escape/symlink, partial-failure, and clean-adopter lifecycle tests prove the public behavior; the Japanese assessment cannot clear the blocker from source-marker presence alone.

A9: Japanese installation guidance, Installed Lifecycle, Capability Truth Matrix, and regenerated Japanese assessment state the exact facts/proposal/execution/receipt results, retain the purge STOP boundary, and clear JA-UNINSTALL-RUNTIME-001 only when the clean-adopter lifecycle test passes.

A10: Plan, Contract, implementation, tests, generated assessment, and acceptance evidence are mapped bidirectionally; full quality, archive, one PR, Hosted CI including terminal evidence, merge, ai-close-work-item, branch deletion, and synchronized clean main complete before documentation alignment begins.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: A proposal is confirmed and no managed path changed after facts collection.
scenarioCoverage.expected: The installed detached executor removes only the exact bound runtime paths, preserves evidence/project-owned paths, writes a receipt outside the deletion set, and verifies post-state.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Create a clean adopter fixture, generate facts and proposal through installed Make targets, execute by exact digest, and assert filesystem plus receipt state.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: A managed file, proposal field, repository identity, or confirmation digest changes before execution.
scenarioCoverage.expected: Execution fails before the first deletion and records the mismatch without mutating the repository.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Mutation-test facts, proposal, repository identity, file digest, deletion list, and confirmation digest.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: A candidate is absolute, escapes the repository, traverses a symlink, is unknown-owned, or is not catalog-managed.
scenarioCoverage.expected: Facts/proposal/execution fail closed and no external or unlisted path is touched.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Use temporary repositories with traversal, absolute, symlink, and unlisted candidates and assert byte-for-byte no mutation.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: Filesystem removal fails after one or more earlier paths were removed.
scenarioCoverage.expected: The executor stops, records a partial non-success receipt with exact actual state and recovery guidance, and never sets runtimeRemovalVerified.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Inject a deterministic removal failure after an earlier successful removal and validate receipt truth.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: The runtime scripts and Make targets are installed into a clean adopter repository.
scenarioCoverage.expected: Facts, proposal, and execute commands run using installed files only, and the Japanese assessment clears JA-UNINSTALL-RUNTIME-001 from executable lifecycle evidence.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Extend installer and Japanese adopter lifecycle tests, regenerate assessment, and run the focused suite plus full quality.

guidelines: Use Python standard-library primitives and repository-relative normalized paths.
Keep facts/proposal generation non-mutating except for their explicitly requested output files.
Require exact proposalDigest confirmation and immediate pre-mutation revalidation.
Never follow symlinks or remove project-owned, evidence, modified, unknown-owned, protected, unlisted, absolute, or escaping paths.
Write truthful durable receipts outside the deletion set for success, block, and partial failure.
Document only installed, executable behavior and retain explicit unsupported boundaries.
Use red-first tests for every destructive and fail-closed scenario.
Record discovered implementation or process problems in the Summary before continuing.

intent.problem: The Japanese release assessment proves that adopter repositories can generate only an uninstall proposal/state output. They cannot build authoritative uninstall facts, bind confirmation to a proposal digest, invoke an installed detached filesystem-removal executor, or verify actual removal. The existing detached module is a non-installed in-memory model, so documentation or marker checks alone cannot safely clear the mandatory Japanese release blocker.
constraints: Preserve evidence and project-owned content by default.
Do not implement purge in this Work Item.
Do not delete any path that was not catalog-managed, facts-bound, proposal-bound, repository-confined, unchanged, and explicitly confirmed.
Keep all real mutation tests inside disposable temporary repositories.
Do not enter documentation alignment or release while JA-UNINSTALL-RUNTIME-001 remains blocked.
Complete one Work Item, one branch, one PR, merge, closure, and branch cleanup before the next Work Item.
intent.rationale: A three-stage facts/proposal/detached-execution protocol with deterministic identity binding and post-state receipts turns the existing conceptual model into reviewable installed behavior while preserving fail-closed control. Executable adopter evidence, rather than source markers or claims, is the only acceptable basis for clearing the release blocker.

restrictedWriteApproval.reason: The user authorized continuous implementation of the Japanese corrective and all required process changes. This approval is bounded to adding the installed ai-cockpit-uninstall-facts, ai-cockpit-uninstall-propose, and ai-cockpit-uninstall-execute public targets to the template-maintenance root Makefile and updating the reviewed Bandit low-risk baseline for the executor's two expected LOW findings; it does not authorize release, purge, unrelated Make behavior, or suppression of medium/high findings.
